thread:
Maya: Quick follow-up from today's design review — the right-hand Help drawer shows the heading "Batching suggestions" but our docs use "Batching & caching". When users click "Read more" they sometimes land at the top of the docs (no anchor), which is confusing.

Ravi: Yep. That's because the drawer links are relative and our docs SPA sometimes strips hashes. We should link to the full docs URL including the hash. Also we should standardize the label. I propose using the docs title "Batching & caching" as canonical but use "Batching" in the drawer UI to save space.

Jules: Design note: long labels look bad in the narrow drawer. We can show the short label and provide a tooltip with the full title, plus visually-hidden text for screen readers like "opens in new tab".

Felix: Accessibility notes: if the link opens in a new tab, add rel="noopener noreferrer" and set aria-label like "Batching & caching (opens in new tab)". Also the docs page needs to move focus to the anchor after navigation so keyboard/VO users have context.

Nia: On the docs side, the router currently hijacks navigation and sometimes loses the hash. I'll add a small fix so the router preserves and processes location.hash on mount. We can also add alias H2 ids for legacy terms (#batching-suggestions, #batching-strategies) that point to the main #batching-caching anchor with a short note about the rename.

Maya: UX copy suggestion for the drawer list: show "Batching" and the link label "Read full guidance". For screen readers, include a visually-hidden span: "Batching & caching docs, opens in new tab". Thoughts?

Ravi: Sounds good. Implementation checklist for console: 1) update drawer links to absolute URL + hash; 2) add target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"; 3) supply aria-label via Link component token.

Jules: I'll update the Link component to accept externalAccessibilityLabel prop and add tooltip support to the drawer. Also will update Figma tokens so designers use the short label in tight spaces.

Felix: Docs implementation checklist: 1) preserve hash on route transitions; 2) after navigation, call focus on the anchor element and ensure tabindex=-1 is set; 3) account for sticky headers when scrolling. Sample snippet I recommend: 
```
const id = location.hash?.slice(1);
const el = document.getElementById(id) || document.getElementById('main');
if (el) { el.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1'); el.scrollIntoView({block: 'start'}); el.focus({preventScroll: true}); }
```

Nia: I'll make a small focus util and add it to the docs router mount hook. Also will add the alias anchors and a short paragraph explaining the rename so old links don't surprise users.

Maya: Can someone own the console changes + e2e? We should add a keyboard test that opens the drawer, tabs to the link, activates it, and asserts the docs page main content receives focus.

Ravi: I'll take the console updates and e2e (ETA 4 days).

Jules: I'll take the design tokens + Link component change (ETA 3 days).

Nia: I'll do docs router + alias anchors + focus util (ETA 2 days).

Felix: I'll do the accessibility review and confirm NVDA/VoiceOver behavior in the pairing session.

docs-bot: Created task #4976: "Normalize 'Batching & caching' across console and docs; add alias anchors and focus behavior for in-app help links" assigned to Nia, Ravi, Jules.

Maya: Thanks team. After PRs land let's schedule a 30-min pairing session to verify keyboard + screenreader behavior. :thumbsup:
